description:
We are a team of ambitious students from the American School of Palestine, passionate about technology, space exploration, innovation, and solving real-world problems. Our experience includes winning the 2026 National Tech Talent Challenge, developing an AI-powered educational platform, building websites, and participating in NASA-related innovation challenges.

We bring creativity, leadership, problem-solving, and entrepreneurial experience.
summary:
LAMOON is an interactive 3D educational game designed to help children aged 7–12 experience the challenges of living on the Moon.

LAMOON puts players in charge of a lunar base with four astronauts. Across five progressively challenging levels, players must manage oxygen, water, food, and electricity while responding to equipment failures and space-weather emergencies.

Through guided missions, colorful animations, interactive repairs, and multiple-choice challenges, children learn how essential lunar systems work and why astronauts depend on them. The game incorporates NASA-supported scientific concepts, including life-support systems, water recycling, solar power, and radiation protection, while simplifying complex processes for younger learners.

LAMOON addresses the challenge by transforming space science into an engaging, hands-on learning experience. Rather than simply reading about lunar exploration, children make decisions, solve problems, and discover how different systems work together to keep astronauts safe.

Our goal is to inspire the next generation of astronauts, scientists, and engineers by making space exploration accessible, understandable, and fun.
details:
LAMOON is an interactive 3D Moon survival game designed for children aged 7–12.

Players manage a Moon base with four astronauts, making sure they have enough oxygen, water, food, and electricity. Across five levels, children explore the base, solve problems, repair equipment, and learn about space through fun challenges.

We built LAMOON using React, TypeScript, Three.js, and React Three Fiber, with GitHub for teamwork and OpenAI Codex to assist development. We used NASA resources to make the educational content scientifically grounded.

What makes LAMOON special is that children learn by playing, not just reading. We focused on simple instructions, colorful animations, fair challenges, and making the game easy to understand.

Our goal is to make space science fun and inspire children to become future astronauts, scientists, and engineers.
